rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb is understood as repeated, gradual descent: the angels keep descending.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-i muzâri‘, aslı تـَتـَنـَزَّلُ’dür. Yani iner de iner: peyderpey iner

rows.speaker: Şihâb
rows.claim: One grammatical reading makes the pronoun in fīhā refer to the night, with the Spirit coordinated with the angels.
rows.anchor: Birisi “leyle”ye[^1] râci‘olmasıdır ki, bu surette “Rûh” melâikeye mâtuf olarak

rows.speaker: Şihâb
rows.claim: Another reading refers the pronoun to the angels and treats the waw as circumstantial: the Spirit is among them as they descend.
rows.anchor: İkincisi, “melâike”ye râci‘vâv da hâliye olmaktır ki, “Rûh içlerinde olarak melâike iner”

rows.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the Spirit as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin kavline göre “Rûh”tan murad Cibrîl’dir

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some identify the Spirit as a mighty angel so vast that the heavens and earth would be a morsel to him.
rows.anchor: Bazıları da “Rûh” büyük bir melektir ki semâvât ve Arz’ı yutsa ona bir lokma olur demişler

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some understand rūḥ as revḥ, meaning divine mercy, as in Joseph 12:87; other views are also mentioned.
rows.anchor: Burada وَلَا تَا۟يْـَٔسُوا۟ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ [Yûsuf 12/87] gibi revh u rahmet mânasına olduğunu da söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever its identity, the Spirit is understood as a category more specific than the angels.
rows.anchor: Her hâlde bundan “Rûh”un melâikeden ehas olduğu anlaşılır

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the angels descend to the lowest heaven; the author finds descent to earth and to those receiving Laylat al-Qadr more apparent.
rows.anchor: Bazıları bunların semâ-i dünyaya indiğini söylemişlerse de zâhir, arza ve kadre mazhar olan kimselere inmeleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Rabb is singular and the possessive pronoun plural, the translation means Allah, the angels’ Lord, not multiple lords.
rows.anchor: âyette “Rab” müfred, muzâf-ı ileyhi olan “hüm” zamiri cemi‘dir. Lisânımızda “Rablerinin” diye tercemesinde “Rab” cemi‘imiş gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly saying they descend by their Lord’s permission stresses the event’s special importance, since angelic descent is already by God’s command.
rows.anchor: melâikenin nüzûlü Allah’ın emriyle olduğu mâlum iken bunu tasrîhin fâidesi bu işin bilhassa ehemmiyet ve azametine tenbihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible attachment makes min kulli amr modify tanazzalu: the angels descend for every decree assigned for execution that night.
rows.anchor: Evvelkine göre ecliyye olarak تَنَزَّلُ’ye müte‘allik, yani “o gece infâzına takdir ta‘alluk eden her emir için demektir” deniliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers attaching the phrase to permission: the angels descend by permission for every decree, encompassing good and matters of religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh “izn”e müte‘allik[^3] olması daha yakındır. “Hep hayra müte‘allik veya dine ve dünyaya müte‘allik infaz olunacak her emirden izniyle”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universal permission matters because this is the night that determines future outcomes, so the angels descend for every decree rather than one specific matter.
rows.anchor: Zira bu gece ilerisi için hâkim, her türlü mukadderâtın tâyin ve tefrîki gecesi olduğundan sâir evkātta olduğu gibi sade bir emr-i mahsûsa müte‘allik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In light of the Spirit being from the Lord’s command, the phrase may allude to the Greatest Spirit descending with the angels; 16:2 is also relevant.
rows.anchor: “Rûh” emr-i rabbânîden olduğu cihetle burada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām means pure safety, a greeting from God, or angels greeting believers; tied to every decree, it can mean safety from every fear.
rows.anchor: Bir selâm yani mahz-ı selâmettir. Yahut taraf-ı ilâhîden bir selâmdır. Melâike mü’minlere selâm verir dururlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One syntax makes salām the fronted predicate and hiya the delayed subject, requiring no pause after salām.
rows.anchor: Bu mânaya göre سَلَٰمٌ mukaddem haber, هِىَ muahhar mübtedâdır. Bu takdirde سَلَٰمٌ’da vakfedilmemek lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A transmitted reading permits pausing after salām, treating it as the predicate of an omitted subject and hiya as a separate subject-predicate sentence.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olarak سَلَٰمٌ üzerine vakıf da tecviz edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grammatical objection about fronting a verbal noun’s complement is answered by the recognized exception for adverbs.
rows.anchor: Masdarın ma‘mûlünü takdim câiz olmadığı hakkındaki kā‘ide-i nahviye ile olan itiraza zarfların bundan istisnâsıyla cevap verilmiş olduğu da meşhurdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He sees salām as an interrupting greeting sentence, like Hūd 11:69, from the angels or God; the central meaning is reassurance of good and safety.
rows.anchor: bize öyle geliyor ki burada “selâm”, قَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًۭا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌۭ [Hûd 11/69] kavlindeki “selâm” gibi haberi mahzuf mübtedâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse removes any implication that the night’s intense pressure or universal decrees could bring harm to the Prophet and community, affirming only good and safety.
rows.anchor: ve herhangisi olursa olsun asıl murad kadir gecesinin mutazammın olabileceği bir tazyik mefhûmundan veya emrin umûmundan dolayı Peygamber ve ümmetine bir şerr ü zarar

rows.speaker: Tîbî
rows.claim: Tibi and others reject pausing after salām, arguing that saying the night lasts until dawn adds nothing because every night lasts until morning.
rows.anchor: Tîbî gibi bazıları سَلَٰمٌ’da vakfı tecviz etmemişler ve demişlerdir ki: “Bu surette هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ beyânının bir fâidesi olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers that until dawn signals the exceptional good and safety lasts all night, and reads hatta as extending the ruling rather than excluding what follows.
rows.anchor: fevkalâde olan hayr u selâmetin bazı saatlere münhasır olmayıp sabaha kadar mümted olduğu, lâzım-ı fâide-i haber kabîlinden olarak, iş‘âr edilmek fâidesi bulunacağı inkâr olunamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ repeated descent with responsibility for decrees gives the earth extraordinary spiritual pressure, yet the night remains good and safe until morning.
rows.anchor: her emirden me’mûriyeti hâiz melâikenin ve Rûh’un peyderpey nüzûlüyle Arz üzerinde büyük bir tazyik husûle getiren fevkalâde büyük bir rûhâniyete mazhar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daybreak is all the more certainly good and safe; dawn, morning, and spreading daylight are conventionally signs of glad tidings.
rows.anchor: fecrin tulû‘u ve sabahın isfârı ve duhânın intişârı âdeten bişâret delilidir

rows.speaker: İmam Şa‘bî
rows.claim: As reported by Razi, Shabi says the daytime of Laylat al-Qadr is like its night.
rows.anchor: Nitekim Râzî’nin nakli vechile bu gecenin gündüzünü istitbâ‘etmesi meselesinde İmam Şa‘bî demiştir ki: “Evet gündüzü de gecesi gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that angels abundantly greet and pray for believers.
rows.anchor: Melâikenin mü’minlere selâm ve duasının kesreti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is literal safety, benefit, and good from evils and calamities, including protection from Satan’s domination.
rows.anchor: Şürûr ve âfâttan sâlim olmak mânasına ayn-ı selâmet ve menfaat ve hayr olması ki şeytanın tasallutundan selâmet mânası[^7] da bunda dâhildir

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: Abu Muslim interprets the night as safe from disturbing winds, lightning strikes, and similar harms.
rows.anchor: Ebû Müslim’in kavline göre müz‘ic rüzgarlardan, sâ‘ikalardan ve bunlara mümâsil ezâlardan sâlim olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says every portion of the night has equal merit, avoiding the varying distribution of recommended worship found on other nights.
rows.anchor: Eczâsından her birinde ibadet bin aydan hayırlı olmakta tefâvütten sâlim olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpreting the Spirit as Gabriel accommodates all the meanings discussed.
rows.anchor: “Rûh”un Cibrîl ile tefsîri bu mânaların hepsine sâlihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salām may also be a greeting that announces or conveys safety.
rows.anchor: Yahut selâmet müjdesi, selâmet tebliği olan bir selâmdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other nights distribute recommended prayer unevenly: obligatory prayer in the first third, optional prayer in the middle, and supplication near dawn.
rows.anchor: Çünkü diğer gecelerde farz sülüs-i evvelinde, nefl evsatında, dua seherde olmak müstehabdır[^8]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication on Laylat al-Qadr is recommended; it is one of the times when prayers are answered.
rows.anchor: Şu da mâlum olsun ki bu mübarek gecede dua mesnundur. O icâbet vakitlerinden birisidir

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha asked what to say if she encounters Laylat al-Qadr, and the Prophet taught her to ask for pardon; Tirmidhi, Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah call the report sound.
rows.anchor: sahih diyerek Tirmizî ve Nesâî ve İbn Mâce ve daha diğerleri Hazret-i Âişe’den şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Striving through prayer and other forms of worship is also recommended on the night.
rows.anchor: Kezâlik namaz ve sâir envâ‘-ı ibâdât ile cehd ederek çalışmak da mesnundur

rows.speaker: Süfyân-ı Sevrî
rows.claim: Sufyan says supplication is more beloved than prayer that night, while Qur’an recitation with supplication is good; he reports the Prophet’s Ramadan night recitation, asking at mercy verses and seeking refuge at punishment verses.
rows.anchor: Süfyân-ı Sevrî demiştir ki: “O gece dua namazdan daha ehabdır. Kur’an okuyup da dua ederse güzel olur

rows.speaker: İbn Receb
rows.claim: Ibn Rajab says the most complete practice combines prayer, recitation, supplication, and reflection; the Prophet practiced all, especially during the last ten nights.
rows.anchor: İbn Receb de demiştir ki: “Ekmel olan namaz, kıraat, dua, tefekkür beynini cem‘etmektir

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say taraweeh prayer fulfills the night vigil.
rows.anchor: Bazıları demişlerdir ki teravih ile kıyam husûle gelir

rows.speaker: Enes b. Mâlik
rows.claim: Bayhaqi reports from Anas that the Prophet promised a great share of Laylat al-Qadr to anyone who prays Maghrib and Isha in congregation through Ramadan.
rows.anchor: Beyhakī Enes b. Mâlik radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle rivayet etmiştir

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Müseyyeb
rows.claim: Malik, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Zanjuyah, and Bayhaqi report that attending the Isha congregation on Laylat al-Qadr earns a share of it.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Müseyyeb’den rivayet eylemişlerdir ki: “Kadir gecesi yatsı namazında cemaatte hazır bulunan ondan nasibini almış olur

rows.speaker: İbn Hacer-i Heytemî
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami says it is recommended to conceal having seen Laylat al-Qadr; only those Allah informs attain its full excellence.
rows.anchor: İbn Hacer-i Heytemî rahmetullâhu aleyh Tuhfetü’l-Muhtâc’da der ki: “Kadir gecesini görene ketmetmesi[^16] mesnundur

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: Alusi says seeing the night means observing signs of its distinctive lights or the angels’ descent, or attaining a mystical unveiling whose reality only its people know.
rows.anchor: Âlûsî’nin beyânı vechile zâhir olan budur ki: Onu görmek demek ona mahsus olan envâr ile melâikenin nüzûlü gibi hasâise ilmi ifade eden alâmâtı görmek

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say the night occurred once because the Qur’an was revealed then or Badr was won at its dawn, leaving only its annual honor and memory.
rows.anchor: Kadir gecesi meşhûru vechile Kur’ân’ın nâzil olduğu veya sabahında Bedir zaferinin vukū‘bulduğu gece olduğuna göre, o bir kere olmuş geçmiştir

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some therefore hold that Laylat al-Qadr happened once and has ended.
rows.anchor: Nitekim bazıları onun bir kere olup mürtefi‘olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author follows the majority: because those events coincided with the night rather than caused it, the hidden night recurs each year, most likely in Ramadan’s final ten nights.
rows.anchor: Lâkin kadir gecesi onlardan dolayı değil, onlar kadir gecesine müsâdif olmuş olduğuna göre leyle-i kadir bütün sene içinde gizli olup en ziyade ramazanda[^19] ve en ziyade aşr-ı ahîrde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s excellence suggests Laylat al-Qadr surpasses Friday and Arafah nights, though this comparison is debated.
rows.anchor: خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ âyetinden zâhir olan da bu gecenin seyyidü’l-eyyâm olan cuma ve arefe gecelerinden de efdal olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse would also imply superiority to the Mi‘raj night, but another view gives Mi‘raj precedence for the Prophet and Laylat al-Qadr precedence for the community.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah hakkında Mi‘râc gecesi efdal, ümmet hakkında da kadir gecesi efdal olduğu söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hidden night that rotates through the year lets all major events coincide with a Qadr night and resolves the disputes; the first revelation night is uniquely greatest.
rows.anchor: kadir gecesi sene içinde devreder gizli bir gece olduğuna göre bu azîm vukū‘âtın hepsi birer kadir gecesine tesadüf etmiş olmak bütün ihtilâfı ref‘edecek olan en güzel bir vecih olmuş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 27th night is the most likely annual occasion because it may coincide with the hidden Qadr night’s yearly return, which explains the majority view.
rows.anchor: her ramazanın yirmi yedinci gecesi bunun devr-i senevîsi olmak şerefiyle hafî olan kadir gecesine isabeti en ziyade melhuz bulunan bir gece olduğu cihetle ekseriyet kavli burada toplanmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daytime is like the night, so worship and supplication then are also recommended; observing both is more cautious across places with different night and day times.
rows.anchor: gibi dua ve ibadet ile mücahede mesnun[^22] olur. Ki bunda ihtilâf-ı metâli‘hasebiyle husûle gelen tefâvüt de bertaraf edilmiş olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since night in one region coincides with day elsewhere, each community benefits by reviving its own night, but counting the daytime too is more cautious for acceptance.
rows.anchor: gündüzüyle beraber hesab olunmak icâbet için daha ihtiyatlı demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding surah’s command means: because the Lord revealed the commanded Qur’an on this night, worship and draw near only to Him.
rows.anchor: O okunması emrolunan Kur’ân’ı böyle bir kadir gecesinde indiren Biz Rabbin Azîmü’ş-şân olduğumuz için ancak Bize secde et ve yaklaş

rows.speaker: Âlûsî
rows.claim: In Sufi usage, Laylat al-Qadr is a special theophany when a seeker recognizes his rank in relation to the Beloved and first enters the station of union and gnosis.
rows.anchor: sûfiyye ıstılâhında leyle-i kadir sâlikin Mahbûb-ı Hakk’a nisbetle kadr ü mertebesini tanıyacağı bir tecellî-i hâssa erdiği gecedir

rows.speaker: İbn Fârız
rows.claim: Ibn Farid poetically says every night becomes Qadr when the Beloved draws near, just as every day of union becomes Friday.
rows.anchor: İbn Fârız bu mânada şunu ne güzel söylemiştir: وَكُلُّ اللَّيَالِي لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ إِنْ دَنَتْ كَمَا كُلُّ أَيَّامِ اللِّقَا يَوْمُ جُمُعَةٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem also hints at the view that Friday is superior to Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: Şeyh’in bu beytinde cuma gününün leyle-i kadirden efdal olması kavline de işaret vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can be partitive or explanatory, attached to an omitted phrase and describing the disbelievers; the syntax permits several ways of dividing the two groups.
rows.anchor: “min” teb‘îziye veya beyâniye, mahzûfa müte‘allik olup كائنين من أهل الكتاب والمشركين yahut الكائنون من أهل الكتاب والمشركين takdîrinde zarf-ı müstekar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording can mean some disbelievers from each group, disbelievers as two groups, or disbelievers who belong to both the People of the Book and the polytheists.
rows.anchor: Bu iki kısımdan kâfirler veya iki kısım kâfirler ki bazısı ehl-i kitab bazısı müşrik, yahut hem ehl-i kitabdan hem de müşriklerden olan kâfirler demek olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading that includes People of the Book who also held explicit or implicit shirk best fits verse 3, which names only them.
rows.anchor: Üçüncü âyette yalnız ehl-i kitab zikrolunmasına bu mâna daha akrebdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are Jews and Christians; naming them this way suggests their rejection of Muhammad and the Qur’an also amounts to rejecting their own Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i kitab Yehûd ve Nasârâdır. Burada “ehl-i kitab” unvânıyla ifade edilmeleri bunlar içinden Allah’a küfredenlerin küfürleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists include all who assign divinity to anything besides Allah, broader than idol worshippers; it includes polytheists and those making their desires gods.
rows.anchor: Müşrikler, Allah tealâ’ya esnâmdan veya gayrısından her ne suretle olursa olsun şirk itikad edenler, yani Allah’tan başkasına ulûhiyet isnad eyleyenlerdir ki putperestlerden e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Allah alone is truly worthy of worship, assigning worship to another independently or in partnership is shirk; multiplicity of attributes with unity of essence is not.
rows.anchor: Vahdet-i zât ile beraber sıfâtın kesreti şirki iktizâ etmez. Şirk ancak zât-ı ilâhda küllî veya cüz’î kesret itikadındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Trinity is shirk and self-contradictory because it claims both plurality and unity of divine essence.
rows.anchor: teslis tevhîdi hakikatte tevhid değil, zatın hem ta‘addüdü hem ittihâdı davasını tazammun ettiği için hem şirk hem tenakuzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lam makes the category general, so polytheists include all kinds; some instead restrict the term to the familiar Arab idolaters of Mecca and Medina.
rows.anchor: Burada لَمْ cins için olarak وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ gerek putperest ve gerek sâire ale’lumûm müşriklere şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects restricting the phrase to known Arab idolaters, since the prior definite phrase already identifies the known disbelievers as some within both broader groups.
rows.anchor: ahd mânası daha evvel ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟’da mülâhaza edilmek kâfîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munfakkin is the predicate of lam yakun, and hatta attaches to it: the disbelievers would not leave their condition before the clear proof came.
rows.anchor: “Münfekkîn” لَمْ يَكُنِ’ün haberidir. حَتَّىٰ da ona müte‘alliktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina denotes an evident proof that makes another matter clear, such as a witness, articulate proof, or miracle; here it is a decisive proof establishing truth.
rows.anchor: Burada da hakkı beyan ve isbat edecek açık ve kat‘î hüccet-i nâtıka veya mu‘cize demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bayyina is the Messenger from God, either by apposition or as an explanation of bayyina through an omitted subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: Allah tarafından risaletle gönderilmiş bir peygamber gelinceye kadar infikâk edecek değillerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purified sheets are free of distortion, suspicion, error, and false doubt, untouched by impure hands; he links them to other Qur’anic descriptions.
rows.anchor: mutahhar, yani tahriften, töhmetten, yanlışlıktan, bâtıl şüphesinden ârî, kirli eller dokunmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sheets contain upright, stable books: enduring true writings, namely the Qur’an’s sheets and surahs commanded to be recited with iqra’.
rows.anchor: onlardadır bütün kütüb-i kayyime yani doğru sâbit kitaplar, bozulmaz, pâyidâr hak yazıları o temiz sahifelerin içindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before a messenger, people could not fully know or unite upon true monotheism and could be excused; after the proof came, the People of the Book had no excuse for persisting in disbelief.
rows.anchor: öyle bir beyyine gelmedikçe tamamen hak ve tevhid dinini bilip de birleşecek ve hâllerini değiştirecek bir vaziyette bulunmuyorlardı ve bunda mâzur olabilirlerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book, or especially their learned readers, divided only after the proof came: some believed, while others persisted in disbelief out of desire and stubbornness.
rows.anchor: Fakat o kendilerine kitap verilenler yani o ehl-i kitab, veya bilhassa onların ulemâsı olan okur yazar takımı

rows.speaker: Vâhidî
rows.claim: Razi reports Wahidi’s statement that this verse is among the Qur’an’s hardest in wording and exegesis, though Wahidi did not summarize the difficulty.
rows.anchor: Vâhidî Kitâbü’l- Basît’te: “Bu âyet Kur’an’daki âyetlerin gerek nazım ve gerek tefsir itibariyle en zorudur

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Razi frames the puzzle: if munfakkin means leaving disbelief and hatta marks an endpoint, the first verse implies conversion after the Messenger, while verse 4 says division followed the proof.
rows.anchor: Sonra infikâkleri ne şeyden, Allah teâlâ onu zikretmemiştir. Lâkin murad, bulundukları küfür hâlinden demek olduğu mâlumdur

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: The preferred Keşşaf solution reads verse 1 as the disbelievers’ earlier pledge to stay in their religions until the promised Prophet Muhammad came; verse 4 reports their failure to keep that pledge.
rows.anchor: Birincisi ve en güzeli Sâhib-Keşşâf’ın telhis ettiği vecihtir

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: On that reading, they promised to unite in truth when the Prophet came but instead split and persisted in disbelief; Razi illustrates this with a sinner who increases sin after becoming rich.
rows.anchor: onlar o Peygamber geldiği zaman hak üzerinde ittifak ile bir kelimede toplanmak vaad ediyorlardı, sonra da haktan asıl ayrılmaları ve küfürde kararları o Resul gelince oldu

rows.speaker: Kādî Abdülcebbar
rows.claim: Qadi Abd al-Jabbar reads the verse as saying the disbelievers would not leave disbelief even after the proof arrived, but the author notes that hatta does not have this sense in Arabic.
rows.anchor: Kādî Abdülcebbar böyle demiş, lâkin lügatta حَتَّىٰ’nın bu mânası olmadığı söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: A third proposal makes munfakkin refer to mentioning the coming Messenger’s virtues: they spoke of his merits before his arrival, then disagreed after he came.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü: Münfekkîn küfürden infikâke değil, beyyine olarak gelecek resûlün menâkıb ve fezâilini anmaktan[^12] infikâk etmedikleri mânasına olmalıdır

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: A fourth proposal says that, after the Messenger came, the whole group no longer remained disbelieving because some believed and some did not, satisfying hatta’s implication of change.
rows.anchor: Çünkü mecmû‘u o küfürde kalmadılar, bazısı mü’min bazısı da kâfir oldular. Bu kadarı da ‘hattâ’nın medlûlüyle amele kâfîdir

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: A fifth proposal says the Prophet’s mission shook their prior certainty in inherited religions; some converted, while others divided through stubbornness despite recognizing their old religions’ weakness.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah ba‘s olununca alışmış yapışmış oldukları eski dinleri hakkındaki cezm ü itikadları mütezelzil ve evvelki fikr ü kanaatleri perişan oldu

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: This proposal distinguishes infikak as detachment from something once clung to from tafarruq as dispersion, showing how the post-Prophet condition differed from the prior one.
rows.anchor: bir şeyin bir şeyden infikâki ona yapışmış iken kopup ayrılması demektir. Tefrika da dağılmaktır

rows.speaker: Fahr-ı Râzî
rows.claim: Razi transmits these five solutions but identifies the first as preferred; the author finds Keşşaf’s wording more subtle and compatible with several proposals.
rows.anchor: Râzî bu beş vechi hikâye ve beyan etmiş olmakla beraber kavl-i muhtâr birinci vecih olduğunu da ihtar eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu al-Su‘ud and others follow the first solution but supply the prior state as the object: their pledge and resolve to believe and follow the last Messenger.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud ve daha birçokları da Keşşâf’ın birinci vechi üzerinde yürümekle beraber “infikâk”in müte‘allakını mukaddemâ üzerinde bulundukları şey

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: The account says the People of the Book prayed for victory through the last Prophet and threatened Arab opponents that they would defeat them with him; later polytheists may have adopted the claim.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i kitabdan bu vaadin vukū‘unda şüphe yoktur. Hatta onlar onunla Allah’tan fütûhât diliyorlar

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: They asked the People of the Book whether Muhammad was the figure named in their scripture, yet after his arrival the People of the Book disbelieved and divided.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah hakkında gidip ehl-i kitaba soruyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds his earlier explanation most apparent: before the decisive proof, people were in a state where they could not leave their inherited condition; after it, the People of the Book should have believed.
rows.anchor: bunu bu esas üzere, yani bulundukları hâlden infikâk mânasına olarak bâlâda îzah ettiğimiz diğer bir vech ile anlamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge reading is awkward when extended to polytheists; reading the object as their religions or disbelief would imply they should depart from them, though the proof was sent for that purpose.
rows.anchor: Ancak bunu o vaad ve azm ile tefsir etmek Sûre-i Bakara âyetine muvâfık olsa da müşriklere teşmîli itibariyle biraz dolambaçlı geliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before Muhammad’s mission was a period of interruption when religions were corrupted, pagans and non-pagans mixed, and truth and falsehood could not be distinguished.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden önceki zaman dinlerin tahrif ve teşvîşe uğradığı müşrikle gayr-i müşrikin karıştığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the rule that punishment does not come before a messenger, the interval is an excuse period without responsibility; before decisive proof, the default is to leave people in their existing state.
rows.anchor: Fetret zamanları ise وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًۭا hükmüne[^22] nazaran mes’ûliyet teveccüh etmeyen bir mazeret zamanı demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets are sent to illuminate truth and duty during such periods, distinguishing believers and disbelievers so accountability can apply.
rows.anchor: Ve beşeriyetin böyle hakk u bâtılı seçemeyecek bir fetret ve zulmet içinde kaldığı zamanlardır ki taraf-ı ilâhîden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the previous surah’s account of revelation’s wisdom, this surah explains the pre-Prophetic interval: before Qur’an and Messenger the disbelievers could be excused, but after proof, especially the People of the Book’s rejection and division, they deserved punishment.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın inzâliyle beyyine-i ilâhiye olan Resûlullah’ın bi‘setinden evvel ehl-i kitabdan ve müşriklerden bulunan kâfirler bulundukları hâllerinden ayrılmamakta mâzur olsalar da, hak dini beyan eden bu beyyine geldikten sonra

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the earlier Torah and Gospel as well as the Qur’an, their duty was to worship Allah alone, without serving another motive or purpose.
rows.anchor: gerek evvelki kitaplarında, Tevrat ve İncil’in esasında ve gerek bu Kur’an ile me’mur oldukları vazifeleri bu idi ki başka bir garaz ve maksada hizmet etmesinler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere religion means directing pure intention exclusively to Allah, without shirk or using worship to serve an ulterior purpose, and seeking reward from Him.
rows.anchor: dini ona hâlis kılarak hiçbir şirk şâibesi karıştırmaksızın şu veya bu garaza âlet etmeksizin sâfî ve temiz niyet ve ihlâs ile ancak O’na tevcih ve tahsis ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif is a distinctive description of Islam in belief, ethics, and social life; it often contrasts Abraham’s religion with polytheism and elsewhere emphasizes pure monotheism.
rows.anchor: “hunefâ” “hanîf”in cem‘i olarak İslâm’ın akide ve ahlâk ve ictimâ‘iyet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here hanif reinforces sound, upright monotheism and sincerity; hanifism is the creed of all prophets, not Abraham alone.
rows.anchor: haniflik Hazret-i İbrâhim’in din ve milletinin vasfı olmakla beraber yalnız ona mahsus değil, umumiyetle müşrikliğin zıddı olarak bütün enbiyânın milleti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hajj 22:30–31 and Shura 42:13 tell prophets to avoid idols and false speech, establish one religion, and not divide; this summarizes hanifism as sincere monotheism and steadfastness.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Hac’da فَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ ٱلرِّجْسَ مِنَ ٱلْأَوْثَٰنِ وَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ قَوْلَ ٱلزُّورِ حُنَفَآءَ لِلَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِۦ

rows.speaker: Şehristânî
rows.claim: Shahristani uses hunafa broadly as the opposite of all polytheists and aligns that category with the Sabians.
rows.anchor: Şehristânî Milel ü Nihal’de “hunefâ”yı ale’l-umûm müşriklerin mukabili olmak üzere ma‘nâ-yı e‘ammıyla Sâbiîlere tekabül ettirerek zikretmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the broad sense, Sabianism is described as the ancient religion underlying polytheism.
rows.anchor: Ma‘nâ-yı e‘ammıyla Sâbiîlik ise ale’l-umûm [5998] müşrikliğin esası olan eski dindir

rows.speaker: Bazı yeni eserler
rows.claim: Some newer works call the old Sabian religion Cybele and say the ancient Hittites belonged to it.
rows.anchor: Şimdi bazı yeni eserlerde buna Seybele-Ceybele [Kybele] dini denildiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hanif community consists of monotheists who avoid falsehood and are charged to invite others and strive against polytheistic religions.
rows.anchor: İşte hunefâ bütün bu şirk dinlerine karşı dini Allah için hâlis kılmak ve ancak Allah’a ibadet etmek üzere davet ve mücahedeye me’mur olan peygamberlerin milletini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish one religion and avoid division applies across Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad; hanifism means unity in sincere monotheism and uprightness.
rows.anchor: Bunların hâsılı ise haniflik, esnâm ve evsâna tapmak sefâletinden, tezvirden, sahte bâtıl akidelerden ictinab ederek Nûh’un, İbrâhim’in, Mûsâ’nın, Îsâ’nın ve Muhammed aleyhisselâm’ın yaptıkları gibi dini Allah için tevhid ve ihlâs ve istikāmetle doğrultmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanif derives from hanaf, combining inclination and uprightness: turning from error and crookedness toward truth, though it can also simply mean inclination or straightness.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin ve ehl-i lügatın beyânına göre “hanef” meyil ve istikāmet mefhumlarını tazammun eder; asl-ı “hanef” yanlışlıktan doğruya, eğrilikten istikāmete meyil mânasına mevzû‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahnaf can describe feet or toes turned inward, explained as an auspicious usage or through two stages of metonymy; hanif always inclines toward uprightness.
rows.anchor: Ayağının ayası veya baş parmakları vahşiden ünsiye, yani içe doğru mâil olan kimseye “ahnef” denilmesi ise tefe’’ül için veya iki mertebe mecâz-ı mürseldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious uprightness means turning to Allah as a doer of good and consistently following His command after professing Him as Lord.
rows.anchor: Dinde istikāmet de بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌۭ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author generally translates hanif as truth-devoted monotheist, though commentators transmit other definitions.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayı ekseriya “hanîf”i hakperest muvahhid diye tercemeyi muvâfık görmüşüzdür

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets hunafa as pilgrims, defining it by an Abrahamic rite.
rows.anchor: ezcümle burada “hunefâ” İbn Abbas’tan “huccâc” diye

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada defines hunafa as circumcised people who forbid marriage to one’s mother and close unmarriageable kin.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den “hıtanlı (yani sünnetli) olanlar ve ananın ve mahremlerin nikâhını haram tanıyanlar” diye

rows.speaker: Rebî‘ b. Enes
rows.claim: Rabi ibn Anas defines hunafa as those who face the qibla in prayer.
rows.anchor: Rebî‘b. Enes’ten “namazda kıbleye istikbal edenler” diye

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid defines hunafa as followers of Abraham’s religion.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den[^6]“İbrâhim aleyhisselâm’ın dinine tâbi‘olanlar” diye rivayet eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: Ebû Kılâbe
rows.claim: Abu Qilaba defines hunafa as believers in all the messengers, in line with Qur’an 2:285.
rows.anchor: Ebû Kılâbe’den لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍۢ مِّن رُّسُلِهِۦ [el-Bakara 2/285] mûcebince “peygamberlerin hepsine iman edenler” diye

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Others describe hunafa as those who encompass the whole religion, a definition close to Abu Qilaba’s.
rows.anchor: daha bazılarından da جامعين كل الدين “dinin hepsini câmi‘olanlar” diye nakl ü târif edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most transmitted definitions identify examples or traits rather than the concept itself; he prefers defining hanif as turning from false beliefs toward Islam.
rows.anchor: Muhtâr olan târif evvelâ îzah ettiğimiz vechile “bütün bâtıl akidelerden İslâm’a mâil olan” diye hulâsa edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All prophets and scriptures purify religion from false beliefs, establish Islam’s true monotheism and sincerity, and guide humanity to salvation.
rows.anchor: bütün kitaplar ve peygamberler dini yanlış akidelerden tasfiye ederek إِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْإِسْلَٰمُ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three foundations of enduring religion are sincere worship of Allah, establishing prayer, and giving zakat; they are the stable religion described in upright books.
rows.anchor: bu üç esas[^10]: Dini ihlâs ile Allah’a ibadet, ikāme-i salât, i‘tâ-yı zekât

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are unchanging foundations of true religions; prayer and zakat are worship’s roots after faith, while their practical details can vary by prophetic law.
rows.anchor: Demek olur ki bu üç esas bütün hak dinlerinin hiç değişmeyen en muhkem esasıdır. Namaz ile zekât da imandan sonra bütün ibâdâtın[^11] aslü’l-usûlüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If religion requires three pillars, they are monotheism, prayer, and zakat in belief and practice, not a trinity in God’s essence.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde din için mutlaka[^12] bir ekānîm-i selâse umdesi tanımak lâzımsa onu Eb, İbn, Rûhu’l-Kudüs diye mâbudun zâtında teslis ile şirke saparak değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book ignored these commands, lost prayer, followed their desires, withheld zakat, and divided, as in Maryam 19:59.
rows.anchor: şehvetlerinin arkasına düşerek namazı zâyi‘ettiler, zekât vermeye yanaşmadılar, tefrika çıkardılar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the opening phrase may be anaphoric, this verse states a general rule: every disbeliever who rejects the proof, from the People of the Book or polytheists, is eternally in Hell.
rows.anchor: bu, sevk itibariyle istiğrak için küllî olmak iktizâ eder. Zira küfrün hükmünü beyan için kübrâ mevki‘indedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation treats disbelief as itself equivalent to Hellfire because it causes eternal residence there.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir mâna ile küfür, cehennemde hulûda sebep olmak itibariyle

rows.speaker: Bazıları
rows.claim: Some say disbelief and sins are already fire in reality, appearing as accidents in this life but taking their true fiery form in the next.
rows.anchor: Onların bulundukları küfür ve me‘âsî hâli hakikatte aynıyla ateştir. Bu neş’ette araz suretinde zuhur ederse de neş’et-i uhrâda o suretten çıkar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, they are in Hellfire in this world and will remain there eternally in the afterlife; those who reject the proof and divide are the worst of creation.
rows.anchor: onlar o sıfatla muttasıf olanlar, yani o beyyine geldikten sonra ona küfredip tefrika çıkaranlar {هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ} hep şerrü’l-beriyyedirler
